explain the different metrics used in previous works. Trask et al. (2018) calculates a score for each model, where the score is the  $ \frac{MSE_{loss} $ of the model}{ $ MSE_{loss} $ of a randomly initialised model} (with no training). A score of 0 reflects perfect accuracy while a score larger than 100 means the solution is worse than the baseline model. Though this method is good for relative rankings between different models, there is no indication to the relative performance against the gold solution Schlör et al. (2020). Furthermore, a randomly initialised model will most likely have poor performance, so the scaled errors of the other models seem better than they actually are. Heim et al. (2020) measures the median of the MSE with confidence intervals using the median absolute deviation.
